expectedLearning: Whether the current semantic and animation layers can converge without changing accepted choreography or introducing an equation-shaped universal model.
allowedWork: Behavior-preserving type extraction, dependency inversion, compatible facades and decoders, architecture gates, narrow projections, compiler and frame adapter migration, deterministic preservation fixtures, and bounded deletion with closure evidence.
Create stable focused and visual verification entry points and the minimum durable architecture evidence required by the approved slices.

Use brief Theseus context receipts, one independently reversible commit per slice, focused verification on every slice, broad gates at slices 6, 13, 22, and 28, and deterministic visual evidence at slices 6, 17, 18, and 28.
disallowedWork: Do not implement new curriculum or domains or redesign the editor, Workbench, reader, dashboard, or authoring surfaces.

Do not create a universal scene graph, CAS, theorem prover, second runtime or clock, arbitrary code execution, broad aesthetic changes, or delete compatibility without route, review, export, fixture, and reference closure.
Do not pause at slice 17 solely for human review; do stop on unexplained visual or semantic drift. The only planned human checkpoint is after slice 28.
goal: Converge KP's semantic-animation compiler into one enforceable dependency direction, typed presentation seam, canonical sampled-frame convention, narrow asset projections, and classified compatibility surface while preserving every accepted behavior in the gold cohort.
commitCadence: Commit every independently reversible verified slice with exact path staging and its durable Theseus evidence.
stopConditions: H1 PRESERVATION: stop on unexplained semantic, correspondence, lineage, choreography, timing, seek, rewind, native-endpoint, accessibility, route, review, export, or performance drift.
H2 OWNERSHIP: stop if a proposed neutral contract contains DOM, KaTeX node, SVG, pixel, Three.js, WebGL, or concrete renderer-resource state.
H3 AUTHORITY: stop if two compiler stages or projections retain conflicting ownership that cannot be safely classified.
H4 USER-OVERLAP: stop if required work cannot be separated from unrelated user-authored roadmap, thread, or exploratory design changes.
H5 SCOPE: stop before new curriculum, editor redesign, universal scene graph, CAS, theorem prover, second runtime or clock, arbitrary code execution, or unsupported aesthetic generalization.
H6 EVIDENCE: stop before deleting compatibility without complete reference, route, review, export, and fixture closure or when deterministic visual evidence shows unexplained drift.
H7 FINAL-REVIEW: execute continuously through slice 28, then stop for the sole human checkpoint before marking the phase accepted.

Exact routes, review scope, descriptor/card lineage, export targets, choreography source, and endpoint authority are checked against live sources; three focused tests and full typecheck pass.

Two consecutive runs each pass 98 tests; full typecheck passes.

slices.title: Executable-compiler-stage-inventory
slices.summary: Added an executable 11-stage semantic-animation compiler inventory from domain state through renderer adapter. Every representation has one authority, source files are checked, order is acyclic, and presentation/domain IR/frame migration targets are explicit. The focused suite passes 102 tests and full typecheck passes.

slices.title: Dependency-inversion-baseline
slices.summary: Frozen all 26 direct semantic and animation imports from rendering as exact typed exceptions. Each dependency names its intended owner, classification, rationale, and a required retirement slice from s09 through s13; the closure test scans both source trees so new imports fail. The 105-test focused suite, architecture gates, and full typecheck pass.

slices.title: Recipe-and-compatibility-ledger
slices.summary: Added an executable ledger for all ten production equation presentation metadata keys and eight broader compatibility surfaces spanning correspondence, typed-gap fallback, transformation refs, legacy intent, timeline vocabularies, generated operation resolution, cross-surface projections, and module registries. Every entry names a live owner, authors, consumers, status candidate, retirement condition, and required closure evidence. All 109 focused tests and full typecheck pass.

slices.title: Deterministic-gold-baseline
slices.summary: Added an executable five-state visual plan for all nine preservation topics and a stable npm visual command that captures animation stages only while asserting canonical routes, direction, progress, native settlement, and deterministic recapture. Focused 111 tests, full 2069 tests, typecheck, build, visual, and performance gates pass with no explained product drift.

slices.title: Layer-ownership-contract
slices.summary: Defined four monotonic dependency tiers over the executable compiler stages, with adjacent typed public seams and renderer resources forbidden before the concrete adapter. Authority remains separate from dependency tier, KpEquationTransitionIr is explicitly equation-domain rather than universal, and four current location/coupling debts own retirement slices. Five boundary tests, all 116 focused tests, and full typecheck pass.

slices.title: Ratcheting-architecture-gate
slices.summary: Added a semantic-animation import-fitness checker to check:architecture that scans all semantic and animation TypeScript files, permits only exact frozen exceptions, and rejects new static, dynamic, re-export, or require-based rendering imports plus stale/duplicate exceptions. The gate exposed and classified one previously missed nested lazy-pack renderer registration, correcting the baseline to 27 exact entries. Seven checker tests, all architecture gates, 120 focused tests, and full typecheck pass.

slices.title: Neutral-equation-transition-IR-ownership
slices.summary: Moved KpEquationTransitionIr and its constructor into src/domain-ir behind a neutral public API; rendering now consumes that seam and the former rendering module is a compatibility-only re-export with constructor identity proof. Migrated semantic, animation, reader, and rendering consumers, preserved exact serialized output and diagnostics, marked the compiler stage canonical, removed its ownership debt, and ratcheted rendering import exceptions from 27 to 23. All 25 targeted tests, 121 focused tests, architecture gates, and full typecheck pass.

slices.title: Semantic-equation-compiler-ownership
slices.summary: Moved semantic transformation-to-equation-IR compilation into src/domain-ir and exported it through the neutral public API; the former rendering module is now a compatibility facade with exact function identity proof. Migrated animation, editor, reader, tests, and ledger references; added a source-level guard against DOM, SVG, canvas, WebGL, KaTeX, and measurement state; added compiler coverage to the recurring focused suite; and ratcheted rendering exceptions from 23 to 19. All 72 targeted tests, 132 focused tests, architecture gates, and full typecheck pass.

slices.title: Neutral-motif-vocabulary-boundary
slices.summary: Moved motif vocabulary, equation defaults, executable grammar, and transformation-tree composition into the neutral animation domain behind one public API; rendering paths are identity-preserving compatibility facades. Migrated production and test consumers, added a concrete-renderer-resource guard and exhaustive facade export-identity proof, added motif contracts to the compiler inventory, and ratcheted semantic/animation rendering exceptions from 19 to 12. All 43 targeted tests, 134 focused tests, architecture gates, and full typecheck pass.

slices.title: Neutral-utility-ownership

Motion-plan authority is now correctly presentation-owned, its mixed-vocabulary debt is retired, and the rendering-import ratchet fell from 12 exceptions to the 5 slice-13 compatibility boundaries. All 62 targeted tests, 178 focused tests, architecture gates, and full typecheck pass.

slices.title: Close-dependency-inversions
slices.summary: Closed all remaining semantic/animation-to-rendering dependency inversions. Generated cancellation now accepts an injected typed presentation resolver; flashcard and drilldown projections accept a neutral runtime-visual-sample factory; concrete witnessed-annihilation registration moved from lazy catalog loading to the equation adapter composition root. The import baseline is exactly empty and the architecture gate scans 260 files with zero exceptions. All 33 targeted tests, 204 focused tests, 2089 repository tests, typecheck, architecture gates, and production build pass.

slices.title: Versioned-typed-presentation-profile
slices.summary: Defined a renderer-neutral kp.presentation-profile.v1 envelope with an equation-only typed payload for motion, native handoff, cancellation, zero witness, successor, depth, continuants, and balanced-branch scheduling. Version 1 rejects all unregistered extension bags, freezes constructed profiles, and cannot carry semantic transformations, correspondence, or renderer resources. Rendering now consumes the neutral recipe types. All 18 targeted tests, 208 focused tests, typecheck, and architecture gates pass; the architecture gate scans 261 semantic-animation files with zero rendering-import exceptions.

slices.title: Legacy-metadata-decoder

Branch choreography and rendering bindings now consume the decoder instead of reading generic metadata. All 26 targeted tests, 214 focused tests, typecheck, compatibility-ledger closure, and architecture gates pass with zero canonical profile mismatches and zero rendering-import exceptions across 262 files.

Clock rounding is a named shared convention used identically by producer and validator. Five envelope tests plus all 225 focused tests, typecheck, and architecture gates pass; no renderer resources leaked into the envelope.

slices.title: Typed-domain-payload-convention
slices.summary: Added a closed, versioned KpSampledFrameDomainPayload union with equation, graph/diagram, and program-trace attachments. Each family has exact shapes, immutable constructors, unknown-input parsing, schema/domain mismatch rejection, duplicate and reference checks, and JSON round-trip restoration; unknown metadata properties and unchecked domain coercions are rejected. The sampled-frame envelope now accepts only this union and deep-clones its payload. Compiler and layer ownership inventories name the three domain-honest seams. All 11 targeted tests, 231 focused tests, typecheck, and architecture gates pass.

slices.title: Equation-frame-adaptation
slices.summary: Added an equation sampled-frame adapter that maps the existing KpEquationFrame semantic contract into the closed typed equation payload and attaches it to the canonical runtime envelope. Forward and rewind object roles and selector correspondence are oriented explicitly; clock parity and active-transformation closure reject drift. The original equation frame remains the exact public compatibility object, and payload attachment changes no descriptor, diagnostic, child, clock, or endpoint view. All 5 adapter tests, 236 focused tests, typecheck, architecture gates, and 39-state linear-equation visual capture pass.

slices.title: Graph-and-program-trace-adaptation
slices.summary: Added distinct graph/diagram and program-trace sampled-frame adapters. Graph payloads carry scene/entity/relation identities and role-labeled mathematical coordinate samples; program payloads carry trace, source, step, stack, locals, and output. Neither payload owns progress or a clock. Graph direct seek and rewind share the envelope clock and produce identical semantic samples; the program preview now uses the adapted runtime frame while retaining its compatibility view. Updated two stale fractional-linear tests to assert the canonical typed presentation profile rather than removed legacy metadata. All 16 targeted tests, 240 focused tests, 2125 repository tests, typecheck, build, and architecture gates pass.

slices.title: Narrow-asset-projections
slices.summary: Added three explicit read-only projections over KpAnimationAsset: semantic-animation kernel authority, presentation/layout authority, and product manifest/export authority. Every aggregate field has exactly one projection owner, all projections share one immutable identity object, and source collections remain reference-identical instead of duplicating state. Recomposing the projections preserves version-1 JSON serialization exactly and rejects independently forged identities. All 5 targeted tests, 245 focused tests, typecheck, and architecture gates pass.
